The results indicate that the parabolic rate law describes the data well, consistent with corrosion controlled by solid-state diffusion of elements through the sulfide scale. This inference aligns with sulfidation mechanisms reported in the literature [14–18]. The absence of linear kinetics suggests that no spalling or cracking of the sulfide scale occurred. Moreover, the observed decrease in corrosion rate with longer exposure times indicates that the corrosion products form a protective layer on the metal surface.
